title: Part Thirty-Six: Verdict II: What Was Taken, Buried and Kept

sections.brief: Ledger of every documented act c.180-2023 (who, document, target, outcome) drawn from Parts 20-31: Irenaeus, Tertullian, Diocletian's Manichaean and Christian burnings, Constantine's Arius burning and VC III.64-66 edict (Valentinians, search for books), CTh 16.5, Athanasius 367 (no destruction), Decretum, 553, Tours 567/Macon 585, Herstal 779, Ad abolendam, Albigensian crusade, Lateran IV c.3, Toulouse 1229, inquisition, Talmud 1242, Montsegur, Ad extirpanda, Templars, Porete, Gui, Spondent, Eckhart, witches, Index, Bruno, Galileo, Ethiopia 1622-32, Masonry 1738-2023, Bavaria; four kinds of act and the actors; told-vs-record myths table. Figures: compare x3 (ledger antiquity; ledger 1184-2023; told vs record) Updated for Parts 32-35: antiquity rows (391-609), Brigid 1538, Rome 1542, a third ledger table (crowns and colonies 1478-2019), told-vs-record rows on Alexandria, Hypatia, mysteries, Inquisition toll, Maya books, suns, Guadalupe, Isis, Black Madonnas. Figures: compare x4

Verdict on the thesis Book Two tests decomposed into six claims and graded documented / probable / not supported (vt19 method); corrections on timing (Ignatius, Justin, tithe 567/585), variety of inner traditions (Valentinians in churches, Flora's Decalogue, Pistis Sophia code, Cathar hierarchy), ancient burning unsupported, actors; Pagels and critics; Church's stated position (2000, 2004); labelled interpretation passage on the lenses (appropriation-suppression-occultation-recovery, unnecessary institution, Sophia/solve et coagula) with counter-readings (John of the Cross). Figures: compare (six claims graded) Updated for Parts 32-35: wider-form thesis graded in the six claims; fifth correction (scale, actors, preservation); probable continuity under Catholic forms; five wider claims not supported; approved-version reading with counter-readings.

Four routes of survival: buried (Nag Hammadi, Berlin, Tchacos, Oxyrhynchus, Qumran; Askew, Bruce), kept by enemies (Flora in Epiphanius, Refutation, Fournier register, Chinon), kept alive (Ethiopian church, Mandaeans), found again (Ficino, Rosicrucians, AMORC, Doinel, Mead, Pagels, Freemasonry; Magdalene 2016, Galileo 1992); parallels (Kabbalah via ts13, al-Hallaj 922); open questions with what would settle them; closing of the volume. Figures: compare (open questions) Updated for Parts 32-35: Maya codices, quipus, Sun Stone, Templo Mayor; Florentine Codex, Landa, Huarochiri, Codex Borgia; Andean, Maya, Afro-Cuban, Plains, Goan and Japanese continuity; Neoplatonism via Dionysius and Arabic; Inti Raymi 1944; eight new open questions.
